decisions.reason: As a core-adjacent product line that had its own page, it carries sunk development costs and visible prior commitment, so management would more likely retain it and interpret its lower web visibility as integration into the broader offer rather than failure.

Because it supports the firm's announced expansion in automation, management can still justify continued commitment on strategic grounds and attribute any weak traction to the long sales cycles of industrial equipment.

Its weaker public visibility makes it easier to prune than the more prominently launched items, but its closeness to the existing formwork business and prior investment still tilt management toward keeping it.
This product line is tightly linked to the established offer and had been publicly highlighted on its own page, which strengthens escalation of commitment and favors continuation.

Although some overlap with other magnetic formwork items makes it somewhat more vulnerable to portfolio cleanup, the firm's earlier public commitment and sunk engineering effort still make retention more likely than withdrawal.
